title: stop.result.v1: what a Stop answers
description: The answer of run.stop when the run exists: 'stopped' or 'pending'. 'stopped' is answered only on evidence that the run's supervised cgroup holds no process; without that evidence the answer is 'pending' with a reason, never 'stopped'. The first three fields and 'repeat', 'reason' and 'recorded' are what the daemon answers today. 'attestation', 'containment_level' and 'claim' are new in version 1 and optional until lane STOP writes them. A client that meets a 'proof' it does not know treats the run as NOT stopped. A client that meets a 'claim' it does not know shows nothing stronger than the weakest claim it does know.

state.description: The same word as 'code'. It is kept because today's answer carries both.

repeat.description: False for the first Stop asked of a run. True when a Stop had already been asked: the run was already stopped, or an earlier Stop was pending and this one confirmed it.

recorded.description: False when the answer could not be written to the registry. Today the field is present only when it is false; an absent field means the write landed. 'Not recorded' is its own fact: the cleanup answer above is still true.

pending_reason.description: Why a Stop is not confirmed. cgroup_populated: a process is still in the cgroup. confirm_timeout: the check did not finish in time. confirm_unknown: the check gave no usable answer. member_alive: a recorded member process is still alive. cgroup_changed: the record moved to another cgroup while the Stop ran. cgroup_unknown: the launch has not recorded a cgroup yet, so the Stop is kept as an intent. cleanup_error:<Name>: the cleanup layer raised the named error.

attestation.description: The evidence a 'stopped' rests on. proof 'empty' (today): the cgroup named here was read empty and every member listed was gone, at this generation of the record. proof 'removed' (lane STOP): the cgroup directory recorded at launch, identified by its device and inode numbers, no longer exists or is a different directory, as observed at removed_at. A client that meets any other proof treats the run as NOT stopped.

cgroup_dev.description: st_dev of the unit's cgroup directory, read at launch.

cgroup_ino.description: st_ino of the unit's cgroup directory, read at launch.

containment_level.description: How the run was contained when it launched. host_integrated: the engine ran as the daemon's own user in a delegated unit (the only level that exists today). engine_user: the engine ran as a separate operating-system user. contained: the unit also ran with the verified restrictions lane STOP defines. PROVISIONAL: the level names are lane STOP's and wait on a decision.

claim.description: The key of the sentence a surface shows for this Stop. No surface writes its own wording. cgroup_empty_whole_run_unverified: the supervised cgroup was read empty; nothing is claimed about a process that left it. cgroup_removed_whole_run_unverified: the supervised cgroup is gone; nothing is claimed about a process that left it. PROVISIONAL: lane STOP owns the list of keys.
